title: Maximizing over noisy estimates
goal:
Reproduce the toy from Section 4. An agent has `n_actions` actions whose true value is 0. Two independent critics $A$ and $B$ each estimate every action as the truth plus $\mathcal{N}(0, \sigma)$ noise.

Write `bias_estimates(n_actions, sigma, trials, seed)`. Draw `qa = rng.normal(0, sigma, (trials, n_actions))` first and `qb` with the same call second, where `rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)`. Pick `star = qa.argmax(axis=1)` per trial and return a dict of three averages over the trials:

- `"max"`: the mean of `qa.max(axis=1)`, the standard Q-learning target.
- `"double"`: the mean of `qb` at the action `star`, the Double Q-learning target.
- `"clipped"`: the mean of `min(qa, qb)` at the action `star`, the clipped double-Q target (Equation 10).

With 2 actions and $\sigma = 1$ the exact value of `"max"` is $1/\sqrt{\pi} \approx 0.5642$. Every value should be a Python `float`.
hints: Index the rows with `rows = np.arange(trials)`, then `qb[rows, star]` is critic $B$'s value at the action that critic $A$ chose.
`"double"` has mean 0 because $B$'s noise is independent of the choice of `star`.
`"clipped"` takes `np.minimum(qa[rows, star], qb[rows, star])`. The minimum of two estimates can only lower the target, so it sits at or below `"double"`.
